_comment: The closed corpus this server speaks. Text is authored here once and
recorded once per voice by `record.py`; every WAV IS committed, so a clone
can hear the avatar without a credential — see that script and
Two voices, because the avatar has a gender and the voice has to agree with
it. `vql_speech` is the id both halves use: what `--tts vql-speech` asks
Voqalize's own service for in a live call, and what `record.py` asked for
when it wrote `audio/<voice>/`. One row, one id — the recorded voice and the
24000 Hz is what vql-speech emits (`pcm_s16le`, mono). It is not resampled
on the way in: pipecat's output transport resamples to the transport rate
anyway (base_output.py, `_resampler.resample`), so a lossy step here would
Sentences are split the way TTSService aggregates them, because that is how
they arrive at synthesis — one `run_tts` call each. Keep them short, and keep
them about the library: this corpus is the demo script, and the thing a
developer is deciding is whether to use it. Backchannels stay one word. This
avatar listens far more than it speaks, and a *go on* that lands is worth
more here than a paragraph that does not.

sentences.text: Hello.
I'm a talking head for your voice agent.
I'm one line in your pipeline.
An avatar processor, seated between the T T S and the transport.
There is no video model here.
I'm a drawing, moved by a small behavior library.
Okay.
My mouth runs on two clocks.
One predicts from the text, the other measures the audio.
The predicted mouth moves the instant audio starts.
The measured one rewrites it a few frames later, and you shouldn't see the seam.
Three kinds of message reach the browser.
A claim, an action, and mouth cues.
I see.
My states come from the frames you already push.
You emit nothing extra to make me listen.
I never decide what the agent is doing.
The server claims a state, and the audio overrules it.
The whole interface is create avatar, with a mount and a client.
It hands back a destroy function and nothing else.
Go on.
Any T T S works, word timings or not.
Without them I just stay on the predicted mouth.
The renderer has no build step.
Plain modules, no dependencies — what you screenshot is what ships.
I never invent an acknowledgement.
Every nod and every receipt is something your server asked for.
Got it.
I stay deliberately still.
A restless face costs you bitrate and says nothing.
Most of my job is listening.
Watch what I do while you talk, not while I talk.
One moment.
Let me look that up.
That's the whole library.
Keep talking, and I'll start over from the top.
